title: The Second Brake: Competence to Die

scenes.tts: If the gate were the only brake, injected cytochrome c should kill these neurons, even in N G F. Does it?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Second Brake: Competence to Die. A neuron with a closed mitochondrial gate.
scenes.narration: If the gate were the only brake, injected cytochrome c should kill these neurons, even in NGF. Does it?
scenes.caption: If the gate were the only brake, injected cytochrome c should kill these neurons, even in NGF. Does it?

scenes.tts: Mohanish Deshmukh tested this directly, with cultured sympathetic neurons.
scenes.visual: Credit: Deshmukh, 1998.
scenes.narration: Mohanish Deshmukh tested this directly, with cultured sympathetic neurons.

scenes.tts: With a fine glass needle, he injected cytochrome c straight into the cytoplasm.
scenes.visual: A micropipette enters a neuron and releases cytochrome c into the cytoplasm.
scenes.narration: With a fine glass needle, he injected cytochrome c straight into the cytoplasm.

scenes.tts: The injection skips the gate.
scenes.visual: Injected neurons glow with dye. Arrow bypassing the mitochondrion. Label: gate skipped.
scenes.narration: The injection skips the gate.

scenes.tts: First, inject neurons kept in N G F. If the gate is the only brake, what should happen?
scenes.caption: First, inject neurons kept in NGF. If the gate is the only brake, what should happen?
scenes.visual: Question card held over an injected neuron bathed in NGF.
scenes.narration: First, inject neurons kept in NGF. If the gate is the only brake, what should happen?

scenes.tts: They should die. They survived.
scenes.visual: The injected neuron in NGF stays healthy. Label: survives.
scenes.narration: They should die. They survived.

scenes.tts: Now take N G F away for about a day. But keep each neuron's own gate shut.
scenes.caption: Now take NGF away for about a day. But keep each neuron's own gate shut.
scenes.visual: Second panel: a neuron with no NGF for about a day, its mitochondrial gate held shut. Two labels: protein synthesis blocked, or no Bax.
scenes.narration: Now take NGF away for about a day. But keep each neuron's own gate shut.

scenes.tts: Deshmukh did that by blocking protein synthesis, or by using neurons lacking Bax. These neurons were alive when injected.
scenes.visual: The gate-shut, deprived neuron is injected. Clock shows hours.
scenes.narration: Deshmukh did that by blocking protein synthesis, or by using neurons lacking Bax. These neurons were alive when injected.

scenes.tts: Cytochrome c killed them within hours. A control injection did not. A caspase inhibitor prevented the death.
scenes.visual: Three small panels: cytochrome c, the neuron breaks up; control injection, it lives; cytochrome c plus caspase inhibitor, it lives.
scenes.narration: Cytochrome c killed them within hours. A control injection did not. A caspase inhibitor prevented the death.

scenes.tts: So something below cytochrome c release also changes, when N G F is taken away.
scenes.caption: So something below cytochrome c release also changes, when NGF is taken away.
scenes.visual: Pathway diagram: a second, unknown block below cytochrome c, now removed.
scenes.narration: So something below cytochrome c release also changes, when NGF is taken away.

scenes.tts: The change builds up gradually. Over about a day without N G F, more and more neurons respond.
scenes.caption: The change builds up gradually. Over about a day without NGF, more and more neurons respond.
scenes.visual: Schematic, not data: the share of neurons that die after injection rises gradually across about the first day without NGF. No single cutoff line.
scenes.narration: The change builds up gradually. Over about a day without NGF, more and more neurons respond.

scenes.tts: Deshmukh called this acquired susceptibility competence to die.
scenes.caption: Deshmukh called this acquired susceptibility competence-to-die.
scenes.visual: Label on the plot: competence-to-die.
scenes.narration: Deshmukh called this acquired susceptibility competence-to-die.

scenes.tts: What does the change need? Look again at how these neurons were kept alive.
scenes.visual: The two gate-shut panels return, labelled protein synthesis blocked and no Bax.
scenes.narration: What does the change need? Look again at how these neurons were kept alive.

scenes.tts: They made no new protein, yet they became competent. So the change needs no new protein.
scenes.visual: Panel 1: protein synthesis blocked, deprived, injected. The neuron dies. Label: still competent.
scenes.narration: They made no new protein, yet they became competent. So the change needs no new protein.

scenes.tts: Neurons lacking Bax became competent too. So it needs no Bax.
scenes.visual: Panel 2: Bax-null, deprived, injected. The neuron dies. Label: still competent.
scenes.narration: Neurons lacking Bax became competent too. So it needs no Bax.

scenes.tts: So this change is a separate brake, and deprivation removes it.
scenes.visual: Card: needs no new protein, no Bax. A second brake.
scenes.narration: So this change is a separate brake, and deprivation removes it.

scenes.tts: Later work identified that brake. It is a caspase inhibitor called X I A P.
scenes.caption: Later work identified that brake. It is a caspase inhibitor called XIAP.
scenes.visual: XIAP drawn sitting on active caspases, holding them back.
scenes.narration: Later work identified that brake. It is a caspase inhibitor called XIAP.

scenes.tts: X I A P levels fall during N G F deprivation.
scenes.caption: XIAP levels fall during NGF deprivation.
scenes.visual: XIAP level bar falls over hours without NGF.
scenes.narration: XIAP levels fall during NGF deprivation.

scenes.tts: X I A P can hold caspases off, partly because these neurons have little Apaf one.
scenes.caption: XIAP can hold caspases off, partly because these neurons have little Apaf-1.
scenes.visual: Only a few apoptosomes, each a normal seven-spoked Apaf-1 wheel; their small caspase output is covered by XIAP.
scenes.narration: XIAP can hold caspases off, partly because these neurons have little Apaf-1.

scenes.tts: Here is a test of that idea. Keep N G F present, and remove the inhibitor. What should cytochrome c do then?
scenes.caption: Here is a test of that idea. Keep NGF present, and remove the inhibitor. What should cytochrome c do then?
scenes.visual: Question card held: NGF present, inhibitor removed, plus cytochrome c?
scenes.narration: Here is a test of that idea. Keep NGF present, and remove the inhibitor. What should cytochrome c do then?

scenes.tts: Smack is a mitochondrial protein that removes inhibitors from caspases.
scenes.caption: Smac is a mitochondrial protein that removes inhibitors from caspases.
scenes.visual: Smac pulls XIAP off the caspases.
scenes.narration: Smac is a mitochondrial protein that removes inhibitors from caspases.

scenes.tts: Cytochrome c injected along with Smack killed neurons kept in N G F.
scenes.caption: Cytochrome c injected along with Smac killed neurons kept in NGF.
scenes.visual: Injected neuron in NGF, with cytochrome c and Smac, breaks up.
scenes.narration: Cytochrome c injected along with Smac killed neurons kept in NGF.

scenes.tts: Put every result against the two brakes. A neuron dies by apoptosis only when the gate is open or skipped, and the caspase brake is off.
scenes.visual: Condition-by-brake table fills row by row: gate column, XIAP column, outcome column.
scenes.narration: Put every result against the two brakes. A neuron dies by apoptosis only when the gate is open or skipped, and the caspase brake is off.

scenes.tts: Once the caspases run, the dying cell signals to be eaten. Where this has been studied, caspases expose a lipid, phosphatidylserine, on the membrane's outer face. It works as an eat me signal.
scenes.visual: Membrane band: gold phosphatidylserine beads flip from the inner to the outer face. Label: eat me.
scenes.narration: Once the caspases run, the dying cell signals to be eaten. Where this has been studied, caspases expose a lipid, phosphatidylserine, on the membrane's outer face. It works as an eat me signal.

scenes.tts: Microglia and other phagocytes recognise it, and eat the cell.
scenes.visual: A microglial cell binds the exposed beads and engulfs the neuron.
scenes.narration: Microglia and other phagocytes recognise it, and eat the cell.

scenes.tts: The cell is normally eaten before its membrane fails. So its contents do not spill, and the tissue is not inflamed.
scenes.visual: Clean engulfment, no spill. Label: prompt clearance, normally no inflammation.
scenes.narration: The cell is normally eaten before its membrane fails. So its contents do not spill, and the tissue is not inflamed.

scenes.tts: Brake two is on the caspases, and deprivation lifts it without new protein.
scenes.visual: Guiding idea card adds: Brake 2 is on the caspases; deprivation lifts it without new protein.
scenes.narration: Brake two is on the caspases, and deprivation lifts it without new protein.

scenes.tts: This apoptotic route needs both brakes off.
scenes.visual: End card line: this apoptotic route needs both brakes off.
scenes.narration: This apoptotic route needs both brakes off.
